idea: Pop art in the style of Romero Britto: every part of the car painted as its own piece, each its own bright colour and its own pattern, outlined in black.
world: A Miami pop-art canvas. Joyful, loud and friendly: flat, saturated acrylic under a glossy varnish, primary and secondary colours side by side, every section of the subject outlined in black like a stained-glass window and filled with polka dots, stripes, checks or hearts. Nothing is shaded, nothing is sad, nothing is worn. It looks like a toy and a celebration at once.

signature.says: Every part its own. Each of the car's parts (the nose, the side skirts, the sidepods, the engine cover, the tail panel, the fuel cap...) is painted as its own piece of the picture, a different colour or pattern from every part it touches, the way Britto paints a cat's ear, face and body each differently. A black outline runs round every part along its edges and seams, so the car reads as a stained-glass window made of its own parts. The inner car's parts (the wings, the arms, the frames) join in, each a solid colour.

dna.says: Every shape is outlined in black, rounded, and filled flat. Lines are smooth and even, never wobbly or pointed: thick (about 2.5 cm) round the big sections, medium (about 1.2 cm) round a mark, thin (0.5 cm) only inside small marks. Patterns are simple and even, laid in rows: polka dots (about 4 cm dots, twice that apart), stripes (about 4 cm, straight and slanted), checks (about 6 cm), little hearts and stars (about 5 cm). A pattern is drawn in white, black or one other colour on its section's colour, never more than two colours in a section. Rhythm: busy, plain, busy, never two neighbours alike.

colours.name: Orange
colours.job: a secondary: a section, or the stripes on yellow

colours.name: Green
colours.job: a secondary: a section, often with yellow hearts

colours.name: Purple
colours.job: a secondary: a section, the deepest colour, with yellow dots

colours.name: Outline black
colours.job: every outline, the inner car's frame and the tyres: the lead between the colours

colours.name: White
colours.job: the patterns' dots, checks and stripes, and the light in the car

meet: Two colours never touch: a black line always sits between two sections. Inside a section, its pattern sits straight on the section's colour, a clean edge, no outline round each dot or stripe.

surfaces.job: every section and pattern on the body: flat bright acrylic under a varnish
the black outlines, as glossy as the colours
the inner car's parts, each a solid colour from the palette, with black between
the wheels: a colour from the palette, outlined
the tyres: black, as an outline round the whole car
the glass: clear, a slight tint at most

ageing: None. The car is a freshly varnished canvas: no dirt, no wear, no fading. Pop art stays new.

large.what: every part of the body its own colour, outlined in black where it meets the next: the car's own parts are the picture's sections

fullness: Full and busy, but ordered: nearly every section carries a pattern, one or two plain sections rest the eye, and the inner car joins in with solid colours. The car is loud everywhere, never cluttered: the black lines hold it together.
never: Two colours touching without a black line between them
Two neighbouring parts with the same colour and pattern
A colour or pattern carried over from one part onto the next
Metallic, chrome, carbon or any worn finish
A pattern on the plates the game letters (the number panel, the engine cover panel, the nose fin's plate): they stay plain
Words, numbers or a cartoon face
